Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
920 AM PST Mon Nov 23 2026

.SYNOPSIS...23/202 AM.

A few showers will linger off the Los Angeles county coast
this morning. Otherwise, mild and dry conditions are expected
into Tuesday. Light rain is possible again Tuesday night into
Wednesday along the Central coast. Thanksgiving will be dry and 
warmer.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-WED)...23/919 AM.

***UPDATE***

Overall a quiet day aside from the ongoing beach hazards (refer to
the Beaches section for details on that). The weak storm 
overnight dropped less than half an inch of rain, and in most 
areas much less. Today dry but cool conditions with some areas of 
low clouds and fog across interior SLO County and the interior 
mountain north facing slopes. Otherwise, clear skies and light 
winds.

As mentioned below, expecting some Santa Ana winds at times this
week, particularly Tuesday and Thursday. Likely falling just short
of advisories but Tuesday but Thursday maybe low end advisories on
Thanksgiving in targeted areas. Afternoon highs will be rising
each day, peaking Thanksgiving and Friday with highs in the upper
70s to mid 80s for most coast and valleys.

***From Previous Discussion***

Weak ridging and offshore pressure gradients are expected to 
develop over the region on Tuesday. LAX-DAG falls to -2 mb
with minimal upper-level support - thus expecting light offshore
winds with warm and dry conditions. High temperatures in the
60s-70s will be common across the coastal and coastal valleys. 

A decaying cold front will approach the central coast Tuesday
night into Wednesday morning. Current trends in guidance has 
decreased precipitation - with amounts generally 0.10" or less.
For Ventura and Los angeles counties, the chances for measurable
rain are less than 10%. As for temperatures, there will actually 
be a bit of warming for most areas on Wednesday as an upper level 
ridges noses in behind the weak front.

.LONG TERM (THU-SUN)...23/202 AM.

For Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday, the combination of 
a strong upper level ridge (588-590 DM) and weak to moderate
offshore pressure gradients will bring warm and dry conditions
to the region. High temperatures will peak on Friday with
coast/coastal valleys reaching mid 70s to lower 80s and about
10 degrees cooler across interior sections. Most locations
will average 8-12 degrees above seasonal norms. Northeasterly
winds are expected to remain below advisory levels due to
limited upper level support. However, there could be some local
gusts in the 40-45 mph range Thursday morning across the 
western San Gabriels and Santa Susanna mtns. A very low chance
that a wind advisory will be needed. 

There is a strong signal that troughing will return to the area
at the end of the month heading into December. We will have to
keep an eye on the potential for a series of systems but details
are blurry this far out. Stay tuned for updates.

&&

.AVIATION...23/1709Z.

At 1600Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Overall, high confidence in majority of 18Z TAFs as VFR conditions
are expected through the period.

The only exception will be KPRB where timing of dissipation of 
IFR CIGs this morning could be +/- 1 hour of current 18Z forecast 
and only moderate confidence in return of VLIFR conditions 
tonight.

KLAX...High confidence in 18Z TAF as VFR conditions are expected
through the period. No significant easterly wind component is
expected. 

KBUR...High confidence in 18Z TAF as VFR conditions are expected
through the period.

&&

.MARINE...23/909 AM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current
forecast. Today through Tuesday, high confidence in winds and seas
remaining below Small Craft Advisory (SCA) levels. For Wednesday
through Friday, high confidence in SCA level seas (peaking between
14 and 18 feet on Wednesday) and moderate confidence (40-60%
chance) in SCA level winds developing on Wednesday and Thursday.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Today through Tuesday, high
confidence in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels. For
Wednesday through Friday, high confidence in SCA level seas
(peaking between 11 and 15 feet on Wednesday) and a 30% chance of
SCA level winds. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Today through Tuesday, high 
confidence in seas remaining below SCA levels. For Wednesday
through Thursday, there is a 50-60% chance of SCA level winds and
a 30% chance of SCA level seas. For Friday, high confidence in
winds and seas remaining below SCA levels.
